reason: This book's mandate is real-asset carry for a confirmed inflationary hiking regime, and on 2026-09-16 the regime stopped being a forecast and became a fact. The Fed raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, unanimously, the first hike since 2023, and 16 of 18 participants now expect at least one more with four seeing two. CPI is 3.4% year-over-year, core PCE 3.3%, WTI is holding $95.71, gold closed at $4,418, the 10-year is at 4.998% and the 30-year at 19-year highs. That is, almost line for line, the world this book was built to own. It would be perverse to tear it up three sessions after the thesis was confirmed. The marks agree: SLV +5.05%, GDX +2.89%, AMGN +2.47%, GLD +2.41%, GILD +1.65%, VLUE +1.61%, MRK +1.35%, XLE +0.44% since the 9/16 fill, with only COMT (-0.69%), USMV (-0.10%) and VTIP (-0.08%) marginally red. The book is +1.45% lifetime on a max drawdown of 3.13% - low-beta carry behaving exactly as low-beta carry should. The VTIP anchor is the leg I scrutinised hardest and it is the leg most vindicated: while short-dated TIPS sit flat at 49.31 with essentially no duration damage, TLT closed at $81.25 against a 52-week low of $80.46 and is -5.71% over one year. Holding the inflation accrual with almost no duration is precisely the right place to be with the curve repricing toward 5%, and swapping it for anything longer would be buying the one asset the hiking cycle is actively destroying. The decision to strip the short-volatility and credit-beta sleeves ahead of the FOMC also proved right - the week's tape showed investors buying only durable-earnings mega-cap tech while industrials, cyclicals and small caps were sold, which is the kind of narrow, defensive breadth in which credit beta and short vol are the first things to break. The one genuine criticism I can level is the 23% combined in XLE and COMT: energy equities were among September's weakest sectors even with crude above $95, a divergence between the commodity and the equities that I am watching. But XLE is green since entry, its 13% stop is live and would take me out if the divergence resolves downward, and COMT holds the commodities themselves rather than the equities, so it is exposed to the price that is actually holding up. That is a leg to monitor, not a reason to pay two sides of friction on an entire $1,000 book. Churn is the real argument here. A full replacement costs about 2bps per side across every leg plus the SEC/TAF on the sells, and it would buy back most of the same exposure under different tickers - paying real basis points to end up in the same regime trade. Idle cash at 13% is already earning 4% APY, which in a hiking cycle is a paying position rather than a drag. Nothing in this week's tape contradicts a single leg, so the correct action is none. Noting for the record that this keeps the Round 3 novelty rule comfortably satisfied: my Round 2 book for 2026-09-21 is semiconductors, memory, E&P energy and short Treasuries and small caps - SMH, MU, AVGO, AMAT, XOP long, TLT and IWM short - which shares zero symbols and zero same-direction gross weight with the eleven long real-asset and defensive legs held here.
